task.description: Hard gate on test coverage for REQ-073's six acceptance criteria. Note: Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER authoring) was merged into Step 2a for this run -- ELIXIR-DEV wrote the design-specified tests directly in the same commit (32c1f4f) that implemented the routes, rather than a separate TEST-DESIGNER handoff. This gate independently verifies the resulting tests regardless of who wrote them.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: end-to-end test per handler (create 201, list cursor page, get 200, patch updated, status-update persisted)
AC2: cross-tenant-404 byte-identical test through the real handler (INV-5)
AC3: tenant-isolation list test seeding both tenants (INV-1)
AC4: permission-denial x3 write handlers, DB-unchanged assertions (not just status code)
AC5: response allowlist test asserting the full key set (not just presence of expected keys)

result.summary:
Ordering deviation flagged (non-blocking, does not affect this gate): WF-02 Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER) was merged into Step 2a -- ELIXIR-DEV authored test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs (23 tests) directly in commit 32c1f4f, the same commit implementing lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex and lib/letflow/identity.ex, rather than via a separate TEST-DESIGNER handoff. Same as the prior two runs this session (REQ-071/072). Validated the resulting artefact independently per my own procedure regardless of authorship.

AC-by-AC mapping, all present and non-placeholder:
- AC1: 'AC1: basic end-to-end coverage for all five routes' describe block (identity_test.exs:74-174), 5 tests -- POST /users->201 with allowlisted shape + DB row confirmed; GET /users->200 cursor page; GET /users/:id->200; PATCH /users/:id->200 + DB-persisted; POST /users/:id/status->200 + DB-persisted status. All assert real HTTP status and decoded body, several cross-check against Repo directly.
- AC2: 'AC2/INV-5' describe block (identity_test.exs:178-202), one test: two real provisioned tenant schemas (tenant_a/tenant_b via TenantFixture), a user genuinely inserted only into tenant_b's schema, dispatched through the real Letflow.Routers.Identity.call/2 for both the cross-tenant id and a never-existed id, asserting byte-identical status AND resp_body. Not a shortcut -- verified directly (see mutation-test finding below).
- AC3: 'AC3/INV-1' describe block (identity_test.exs:268-286), one test: two provisioned tenants, tenant_b seeded with two similarly-named users ('alice','alice2'), tenant_a with its own 'alice'; list dispatched as tenant_a asserts exactly 1 item returned, username 'alice'. Real cross-schema data, real handler dispatch.
- AC4: 'AC4: permission-denial...' describe block (identity_test.exs:206-264), a for-comprehension generating 2x3=6 tests: {no roles, wrong role 'TASK_WORKER'} x {create, patch, status-update}. Create asserts Repo.aggregate count unchanged; patch/status-update snapshot the full row via Repo.get! before the request and assert full-row equality (==) after -- genuine field-level snapshot comparison, not merely a row count, satisfying AC4's explicit 'not only by the status code' wording.
- AC5: covered inside the AC1 create test (identity_test.exs:93-106): asserts each of the 8 allowlisted keys' values explicitly (id, username, display_name, email, status, auth_source, inserted_at, updated_at) AND separately refutes the 3 excluded keys are present (password_hash, external_id, external_realm) via Map.has_key?/2. This is a full-key-set assertion (8 positive + 3 explicit negative on the only other schema fields), not a partial-presence check -- it would catch a leaked 9th key introduced by a real Jason.Encoder derivation as well as a positive-only check might miss, since the three most security-sensitive candidate leaks are explicitly refuted by name.
- AC6: documentation-only AC (moduledoc content), no test obligation per the design's own §1a wording ('a concrete build requirement...CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR...and REVIEWER...check this by reading the real @moduledoc string'). Read lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:1-35 directly myself: all five required lines present verbatim, matching the design's required shape and REVIEWER's step-02d sign-off. No test gap -- correctly a doc-read check, not an ExUnit assertion.

Re-run (myself, real output, not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's 23/23 claim): `mix test test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs` -> Result: 23 passed, 0 failures. Confirmed exactly. Also ran the identity-adjacent suite: `mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs test/letflow/api/context_test.exs` -> Result: 42 passed, 0 failures. No regressions.

No skipped coverage: grepped the file for '@tag :skip' and 'TODO' -- none found. All 23 tests are real assertions on real HTTP dispatch through Letflow.Routers.Identity.call/2 against a real Postgres-backed tenant schema (Letflow.DataCase, async: false).

Fixture isolation: every describe block provisions its own tenant(s) via TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 with a unique slug_prefix per describe block (req073-e2e, req073-cross-a/b, req073-403, req073-iso-a/b, req073-filters, req073-validation, req073-notfound) -- Ecto.UUID.generate() backs the actual schema name, so no cross-test collision even across repeated runs. insert_user!/2 generates unique username/email per call via Ecto.UUID.generate() interpolation. No shared hardcoded IDs found. Tests are self-sufficient: each test's setup block (or the test itself, for AC2/AC3) provisions exactly the tenant(s) it needs; no test reads state left by a prior test. No hardcoded secrets or connection strings -- Repo/tenant access goes through TenantFixture and the DataCase's sandboxed Repo config, nothing literal.

Point 6 (mutation-test judgment on AC2): applied a mutant to lib/letflow/identity.ex's get_user/2 myself (temporary, in-tree, then reverted -- see below) rather than accepting the design doc's structural argument on its face, since that argument is exactly the kind of claim 'Every producing step has a validating step' says must be re-derived, not copied. Mutant: added a fallback unscoped Repo.all query when the scoped lookup misses (simulating a forgotten-scope bug class). Ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs:186` (the AC2 test alone): it failed -- Postgrex undefined_table error surfaced through the handler, because this codebase's per-tenant schema-per-tenant architecture (Decision 0003/0006) means there is no shared/public `users` table an unscoped query could hit, so the mutant manifests as a hard failure rather than a silent leak. This confirms the test is NOT a shortcut that would pass under a broken get_user/2 -- any deviation from the scoped-prefix-only lookup breaks this test, whether via an actual leak (impossible to construct generically here given the schema-per-tenant isolation) or via the crash this mutant produced. Combined with REQ-072's own already-mutation-tested scoped_repo_opts/1 primitive (which this test calls unmodified via the real router->Identity.get_user/2->opts chain), I judge no further mutation testing is warranted here: the underlying scoping primitive is proven at REQ-072, and this test's own sensitivity to a handler/domain-function-level scoping break is now independently proven here too, not merely asserted by the design doc. Reverted the mutant with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/identity.ex` immediately after the probe. Verified revert: `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` -> empty (no output). Verified `mix test test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs` re-runs green after revert -> Result: 23 passed.

No hardcoded secrets/connection strings found in the test file. All checks pass -- PASS.
